action.description: Which operation to perform — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "modify-event" pairs with modifyEvent: {...}).

timeMin.description: Start of time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2026-03-01T00:00:00-07:00). Required — the beginning of the period to fetch events for. If no clear input is provided, use the FIRST DAY of the current year.

timeMax.description: End of time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2026-03-01T23:59:59-07:00). Required — the end of the period to fetch events for. If no clear input is provided, use the LAST DAY of the current year.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID to fetch events from. Defaults to 'primary'. Only pass a different value if the user explicitly asks about a specific calendar.

q.description: Free text search query. Filters events by matching against title, description, location, and attendee names/emails.

startDateTime.description: Start of time range to check availability in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T00:00:00-07:00). Should be the beginning of the day or time range you want to check.

endDateTime.description: End of time range to check availability in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T23:59:59-07:00). Should be the end of the day or time range you want to check.

calendarIds.description: Optional array of calendar IDs to check. If not provided, uses the user's selected calendars from their calendar settings, or falls back to 'primary' calendar.

operation.description: Which calendar mutation to perform. "create" needs summary/startDateTime/endDateTime/attendees. "update" needs eventId plus any fields you want to change. "delete" needs only eventId.

eventId.description: The Google Calendar event ID to update or delete. Required for operation=update/delete.

summary.description: Meeting title. Required for create. For update, provide only to change it. Use format "CompanyName <> CompanyName" if companies are clear, or "FirstName <> FirstName" if not.

description.description: Meeting description. For create, defaults to empty. If there is an agreed next topic, provide 2-3 bullet points.

startDateTime.description: Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T10:00:00-07:00). Required for create. MUST be in the future.

endDateTime.description: End time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T11:00:00-07:00). Required for create. MUST be after startDateTime.

attendees.description: Meeting attendees. Required for create. CRITICAL: ONLY include attendees whose ACTUAL email addresses you extracted from the conversation (headers, signatures, previous messages). ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: making up emails or using placeholder domains (@example.com, @domain.com). Better to have fewer real attendees than fake ones.

location.description: Meeting location. For create, defaults to "Online" for virtual meetings.

wantsMeetLink.description: Whether to create a video conference link. For create, defaults to true when omitted, so leave it out. Pass false ONLY if the user explicitly asked for no video link or said the meeting is in person with no call. If they asked for a link, keep it even when the meeting is at an office. Never pass false on your own judgement.

conferenceType.description: Which conference `wantsMeetLink` creates: `hangoutsMeet` (Google Meet, the default) or `zoom`, which Cedar mints on the user's own Zoom account and attaches to the event. Only set `zoom` when the user asked for Zoom by name; a user who has not connected Zoom gets an event with no video link rather than a failure.

recurrence.description: RFC 5545 recurrence rules to make this a repeating event, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;COUNT=10"]. Omit for a one-time event. Common patterns: daily "RRULE:FREQ=DAILY", weekly "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR", biweekly "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2", monthly "RRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY". Add ";COUNT=n" to stop after n occurrences, or ";UNTIL=YYYYMMDD" to stop on a date — do not set both. For "update", this REPLACES the whole recurrence (reissue every rule you want kept, or pass an empty array to make the series a one-time event). Always affects the WHOLE series — the tool resolves eventId to its series master itself, even if you pass a single expanded instance id from list-events. Other fields on the same update (time, summary, etc.) still apply only to the instance you named, if that's what eventId is.

user_request_summary.description: One sentence, in your own words: what the user actually asked you to do in this turn. Used only for Cedar's observability — it does not change what this tool does.

is_new_request.description: true on the FIRST Cedar tool call of a NEW user request; false when this call continues the same request you are already working on. Groups related calls into one activity thread.
